items.title: Could Mississauga fine your vehicle for lawn parking? Proposed bylaw explains who pays and how disputes might work
items.summary: Drivers — not homeowners — would face the fine under the proposed bylaw. Mississauga councillors are considering a new bylaw to ticket cars parked on lawns. Mississauga is considering a new bylaw to penalize vehicles parked on residential lawns and landscaped areas. According to a report coming to general committee on Sept. 23, staff are recommending a standalone lawn parking bylaw to penalize vehicle owners — not property owners — if a car is parked on a residential lawn. If approved, the bylaw will ban parking, standing and stopping of vehicles on landscaped soft areas such as grass or gardens on residential properties and fines will be set at $150 for standard vehicles and $375 for heavy or recreational vehicles (RV), according to the report. Violations will be handled through the city’s Administrative Penalty System (APS) allowing municipal enforcement officers to directly issue a penalty notice to a vehicle’s owner regardless of who was driving. Registered drivers could dispute the penalty through the APS dispute resolution process, according to the report. Currently, the city handles lawn parking complaints through the zoning bylaw which staff say is time consuming and resource-intensive because it requires an investigation of the property conditions rather than the act of parking. It also requires warning periods, reinspections and potential court proceedings.

items.title: Gun Seized in Cross-Border Trafficking Bust Ties Back to a 2024 Mississauga Killing
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say an undercover operation called Project Red Zone, run by the force's Specialized Enforcement Bureau alongside the US Department of Homeland Security and Criminal Intelligence Service Ontario, infiltrated and disrupted a firearms trafficking network operating across the Greater Toronto Area. According to police, the operation seized 23 firearms, 75 grams of cocaine, and more than 950 rounds of ammunition, along with several weapons that are prohibited in Canada. Investigators say one of the recovered firearms has been linked to a March 2024 homicide in Mississauga in which one man was killed and another seriously injured. Police say forensic analysis also tied the seized firearms to 14 separate shootings across the GTA. The investigation determined that 15 of the 23 firearms had originated in the United States before making their way into the trafficking network.

items.title: Washroom Upgrades This Fall Are Just a Preview of a Bigger Celebration Square Overhaul
items.summary: According to INsauga, construction is set to begin this fall at Celebration Square in downtown Mississauga following the venue's seasonal shutdown, though it is only a smaller step ahead of the much larger renovation planned for the outdoor space. The washrooms at the square will be temporarily closed during the work and are expected to reopen in mid-November. The bigger renovation, covering the nearly five-acre public gathering space, could see construction begin toward the end of 2027, the city has said. Plans for that larger project have grown since 2025, when the city first floated more modest improvements for early 2026, into a significantly bigger renewal that will reshape the venue over the next couple of years. Earlier proposals called for bigger, higher-resolution viewing screens and new artificial turf, with that turf-replacement work expected to close the lawn and surrounding pavement to the public for four to six weeks once it begins.

items.title: Eagle Spirits of the Great Waters hosts Art Mashkiki, Truth and Reconciliation Gathering this weekend
items.summary: All events will take place at the Small Arms Inspection Building. Indigenous regalia, paintings, crafts and more will be showcased at the annual exhibition from Sept. 23 to Oct. 8. The Small Arms Inspection Building will be hosting the seventh annual Art Mashkiki art exhibition from Sept. 23 to Oct. 8. The exhibit is organized by Eagle Spirits of the Great Waters, an Indigenous-led arts and culture non-profit organization. It will showcase artworks, photography, art installations, crafts and more from various Indigenous communities at the 1352 Lakeshore Rd. E. venue. The opening reception is scheduled for Sept. , and will feature performances by Indigenous singers and dancers as well as speakers who will share their teachings and experiences. items.title: City Offices Will Close September 30 as Mississauga Marks Truth and Reconciliation Day
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says it will once again recognize the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation and Orange Shirt Day on Wednesday, September 30, a day meant to honour Indigenous children who never returned home, residential school survivors, and the families and communities still affected by that legacy. According to the city, it remains committed to advancing reconciliation and building awareness and understanding within the community as Canadians reflect on the lasting impact of residential schools. In the lead-up to September 30, the city says it will offer a range of educational initiatives and opportunities for residents to learn, reflect and engage with the history involved. City offices will be closed on September 30 to observe the day, with regular hours resuming Thursday, October 1. Residents can check the city's website for details on what services remain open or closed that day.

items.title: Mississauga’s Top 100 Under $100 standouts: sprawling, diverse and delicious
items.summary: Our team of 11 food experts selected the Mississauga spots that made our Top 100 Under $100 guide. Hisham Amleh makes falafel fried-to-order for peak texture and flavour. Mississauga’s food scene is a reflection of the city itself: sprawling, diverse and shaped by generations of newcomers who have brought their cooking traditions with them. From Pakistani karahi and Palestinian falafel to South Indian dosas, Egyptian comfort food, Indonesian specialties and hand-pulled Chinese noodles, the city is packed with restaurants serving food that rarely feels generic or watered down. Our team of 11 food experts selected the spots below as being extra special: they made our Top 100 Under $100 guide to delicious, affordable restaurants in the GTA. Here are some of Mississauga’s standouts. Let us know what you think. It’s the offshoot of a Lahore mini-chain dating to the 1970s. The recipes, passed down through generations, shape a menu of hearty, shareable dishes. The chicken malai boti is a good place to start: marinated breast turned tender and smoky in a charcoal-fired tandoor oven. items.title: Hospitalization Count from Mississauga Apartment Fire Climbs to 18, CBC Reports
items.summary: CBC Toronto reports that the number of people hospitalized after Monday's fire at a Mississauga apartment building near Inverhouse Drive and Lakeshore Road West has climbed to at least 18, including a firefighter and a Peel police officer. According to CBC, residents of the building were left shaken by the blaze, which broke out in a hallway and forced an evacuation. Peel Regional Police say the fire may have been arson, though investigators had not confirmed a cause as of Monday. The higher count marks an increase from earlier same-day estimates that had put the number of people treated closer to 10 or 11, suggesting more people were assessed for smoke inhalation and other injuries as the day went on. The officer and firefighter who were hurt were both injured while helping other residents get safely out of the building.

items.title: Councillors Call E-Scooters a Safety 'Crisis' as Mississauga Lobbies Queen's Park for Tighter Rules
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga officials have escalated their push for the provincial government to tighten regulations on e-scooters, with one city councillor describing the current situation around the motorized devices as a public safety crisis. Mayor Carolyn Parrish said she expects Ontario's transportation minister, Prabmeet Sarkaria, may soon announce that police across the province will get expanded authority to enforce road rules against e-scooter riders. The provincial government is expected to address e-scooters and e-bikes more broadly, with new regulations anticipated sometime this fall. Parrish and Ward 3 Councillor Chris Fonseca were part of a Mississauga delegation that raised e-scooter safety directly with provincial officials last month at the Association of Municipalities of Ontario conference in Ottawa. The city followed up after that conference with letters to the province spelling out its concerns and requests on several fronts. Parrish told council last Wednesday that the Ottawa trip was really productive and that provincial ministers and other officials listened to the city on several fronts, including on e-scooter safety.
